t:
(a) In General.—Section 2380A of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) by striking “Notwithstanding” and inserting the following:“(a) Goods and Services Provided by Nontraditional Defense Contractors.—Notwithstanding”; and 
        (2) by adding at the end the following new subsection:“(b) Services Provided by Certain Nontraditional Contractors.—Notwithstanding section 2376(1) of this title, services provided by a business unit that is a nontraditional defense contractor (as that term is defined in section 2302(9) of this title) shall be treated as commercial items for purposes of this chapter, to the extent that such services use the same pool of employees as used for commercial customers and are priced using methodology similar to methodology used for commercial pricing.”.  
    (b) Conforming Amendments.—
        (1) Section heading.—Section 2380A of title 10, United States Code, as amended by subsection (a), is further amended by striking the section heading and inserting the following:“§ 2380a. Treatment of certain items as commercial items”
. 
        (2) Table of sections.—The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 140 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking the item relating to section 2380A and inserting the following new item:

“2380a. 
Treatment of certain items as commercial items.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mention of nontraditional defense contractors, who are outside parties, signals outside involvement. But the section only reclassifies their services as commercial items for procurement purposes and makes conforming heading and table amendments. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: services provided by a business unit that is a nontraditional defense contractor (as that term is defined in section 2302(9) of this title) shall be treated as commercial items for purposes of this chapter

opus.w: This provision is a definitional procurement rule. It treats certain services from nontraditional defense contractors as commercial items and makes conforming changes to the section heading and table of sections. Contractors are mentioned, but they are not consulted or given any role in a federal decision. Contracting is like applying for contracts, which falls under the definition's exclusions. Nothing here creates rulemaking, a comment period, an advisory body or a right to sue.
opus.s: services provided by a business unit that is a nontraditional defense contractor (as that term is defined in section 2302(9) of this title) shall be treated as commercial items for purposes of this chapter
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this involves outside companies (nontraditional defense contractors and their commercial customers), so it might count as participation. That reading fails: the provision only says how certain contractor services are classified for procurement purposes. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the definition of how services from nontraditional defense contractors are treated under federal procurement law. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making processes. The mention of 'nontraditional defense contractors' is part of a legal classification, not a requirement for their participation in the legislative or regulatory process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that defining "nontraditional defense contractors" involves outside parties, but this is merely a statutory definition and classification for procurement purposes, not a process for consultation or participation in decision-making. The text does not require the government to consult with these contractors or any other outside group before making a decision; it simply changes how their services are treated under existing law.
